chapter_name: Shabd Rachna 1: Upsarg Aur Pratyay (Word Formation: Prefixes and Suffixes)
learning_objective: 🎯 By the end of this chapter, you will become a word-mechanic, learning how to attach front and back bumpers to root words to magically create hundreds of new words!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🛠️ The Word Factory (How new words are made)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: We don't always invent brand new words from scratch. Instead, we take an existing 'Mool Shabd' (Root Word) and stick tiny word fragments (Shabdaansh) to its front or back. This process changes the meaning completely and expands our vocabulary effortlessly!

An 'Upsarg' (Prefix) is a word fragment added to the BEGINNING of a root word to change its meaning. For example, take the root word 'मान' (Respect). Add the Upsarg 'अप्' (Ap) to the front, and it becomes 'अपमान' (Insult)! The meaning completely flipped.

Hindi borrows front engines from different languages! We use Sanskrit prefixes (अति + अंत = अत्यंत), Hindi prefixes (अध + पका = अधपका / half-cooked), and even Urdu/Persian prefixes (ना + पसंद = नापसंद / dislike).

A 'Pratyay' (Suffix) is a word fragment added to the END of a root word. For example, take the root word 'सुंदर' (Beautiful). Add the Pratyay 'ता' (ta) at the end, and it becomes 'सुंदरता' (Beauty - an abstract noun). Suffixes often change adjectives into nouns or nouns into adjectives!

Some special words are so greedy, they take both an Upsarg AND a Pratyay at the same time! Take the root word 'स्वतंत्र' (Independent). Add 'अ' (Prefix) + तंत्र (Root) + 'ता' (Suffix) = 'अस्वतंत्रता' (Lack of freedom). You can also add two suffixes: भारत + ईय + ता = भारतीयता (Indianness).

fun_activity.title: 🧩 The 'Root Word' Extraction
fun_activity.instructions: Be a word surgeon! Extract the 'Mool Shabd' (Root Word) hidden inside these words: 1. असत्य (Asatya), 2. कमजोरी (Kamzori), 3. बेईमान (Beimaan), 4. मित्रता (Mitrata). Write down what is the root, and what is the Upsarg or Pratyay!

quick_recap: ⭐ Upsarg (Prefixes) are fragments added at the BEGINNING of a word to change its meaning.
⭐ Pratyay (Suffixes) are fragments added at the END of a word to alter its grammatical form or meaning.
⭐ Neither Upsarg nor Pratyay can be used independently; they must attach to a valid Root Word (Mool Shabd).
⭐ A single root word can sometimes take both a prefix and a suffix simultaneously.
